meta.title: Support ticket lifecycle
meta.description: The states a support ticket moves through and the event behind every move.

summary.headline: A ticket only changes state on an event; reopening, hand-backs and customer replies send it round again.
points: Triage rejects spam and duplicates before an agent picks the ticket up.
Internal notes loop on Open without changing the state.
Asking the customer and their reply is one two-way move.
A reopened ticket goes back from Resolved to Open.

data.title: Start
data.description: A customer writes in by email, chat or the help centre.

data.title: New
data.subtitle: Not yet looked at
data.description: Created automatically from the incoming message.

data.title: Valid request?
data.description: Triage checks for spam, duplicates and the right queue.

data.title: Open
data.subtitle: An agent is working on it

data.title: Waiting on customer
data.subtitle: Paused until they reply
data.description: The SLA clock stops while the ticket waits.

data.title: Closed
data.description: Archived; a new message opens a new ticket.

steps.title: Overview
steps.description: Seven states between a start and an end. Every arrow is an event; the loop and the back-arrows are the ticket going round again.

steps.title: Intake and triage
steps.description: A message creates a New ticket. Triage decides: valid tickets open, spam and duplicates are rejected.

steps.title: Working the ticket
steps.description: Internal notes keep the ticket Open (the loop). Asking the customer pauses it in Waiting; their reply brings it back (one two-way arrow).

steps.title: Escalation
steps.description: Hard problems go to engineering and come back to the same agent with an answer.

steps.title: Resolve or reopen
steps.description: Sending the fix resolves the ticket. If the customer says it is not fixed, it reopens.

steps.title: Close
steps.description: Resolved tickets close after seven quiet days; rejected ones close at once.
